steps.title: Import Vue and ref from vue
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary Vue functionality.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing from a package
import { ref } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue framework and ref function are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Vue and ref, which are essential for creating reactive state in Vue components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Remember to import Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create the main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create and export a default Vue component named 'DebouncedSearch' that returns a template with a single root element.
steps.hint: Use the Vue defineComponent function to create a component. Remember to export it as default.
steps.seedCode:
import { defineComponent } from 'vue';

// Create and export the DebouncedSearch component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named DebouncedSearch is defined and exported as the default export.
successCriteria: The component is named 'DebouncedSearch', uses defineComponent, and is exported as default.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main Vue component for the debounced search feature.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the component is named 'DebouncedSearch' and exported as default.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you used defineComponent and exported it as default.

steps.title: Initialize search query state with ref
steps.instruction: Inside the component, declare a reactive searchQuery variable using ref and initialize it with an empty string.
steps.hint: Use the ref function imported from 'vue' to create reactive state.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example reactive state declaration
const count = ref(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have reactive state ready to store the user's search input.
successCriteria: A searchQuery variable is declared using ref with an empty string initial value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created reactive state for the search query.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref() with an empty string as the initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The searchQuery state wasn't properly initialized. Remember to use ref() from Vue.

steps.title: Initialize search results state with ref
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a reactive searchResults state variable using ref and initialize it with an empty array.
steps.hint: Use the ref function imported from 'vue' to create reactive state. Initialize it with [] for an empty array.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: reactive array state
const items = ref([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a reactive searchResults state variable initialized as an empty array, ready to store search results.
successCriteria: searchResults is declared using ref with an empty array as initial value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a reactive searchResults state variable. This will hold the search results that we'll fetch later.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using ref() with an empty array [] as the initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a reactive variable called searchResults using ref() and initialize it with an empty array.

steps.title: Create a mock search function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a function named performSearch that takes a query parameter and returns mock search results.
steps.hint: Define a function that filters a static array of mock data based on the query.
steps.expectedOutcome: A performSearch function is defined in the setup function, ready to be used for filtering mock data.
successCriteria: The performSearch function is created, takes a query parameter, and returns filtered results from mock data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the mock search function. This function will simulate searching through data based on the query.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the function is named performSearch, takes a query parameter, and returns filtered results from mock data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or incorrectly defined. Create a function named performSearch that filters mock data based on the query parameter.

steps.title: Create the search handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a function named handleSearch that takes an event parameter, updates searchQuery with the input value, and calls performSearch.
steps.hint: Define handleSearch to update the reactive state and trigger the search logic.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a handleSearch function that will be used to respond to input changes.
successCriteria: A function named handleSearch is defined, updates searchQuery.value, and calls performSearch.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the search handler function that updates the query and triggers the search.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it updates searchQuery.value and calls performSearch.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleSearch function is missing or doesn't update the state and call performSearch.

steps.title: Create the debounce function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a debounce function that takes a callback function and a delay time as parameters, and returns a debounced version of that callback.
steps.hint: The debounce function should use setTimeout to delay execution and clearTimeout to cancel pending executions when called again within the delay period.
steps.expectedOutcome: A debounce function is implemented inside the component's setup function, ready to be used with the search handler.
successCriteria: The debounce function is defined with parameters for callback and delay, uses setTimeout and clearTimeout, and returns a debounced function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the debounce function. This will help prevent excessive API calls during rapid typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the debounce function, but make sure it takes callback and delay parameters, uses setTimeout/clearTimeout, and returns a debounced function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The debounce function isn't implemented correctly. Review the example: it should accept a callback and delay, manage a timeout, and return a debounced version.

steps.title: Create debounced search handler
steps.instruction: Create a debounced version of your handleSearch function using the debounce utility you wrote earlier.
steps.hint: Call your debounce function, passing handleSearch as the first argument and a delay (like 500ms) as the second argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a debounced version of handleSearch ready to use in your component.
successCriteria: A debounced version of handleSearch is created using the debounce function with a specified delay.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a debounced search handler that will prevent excessive API calls.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling the debounce function with handleSearch and a delay value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a debounced version of handleSearch using the debounce function you wrote earlier.

steps.title: Add the main template structure
steps.instruction: In your component's return statement, add a template section with a main container div.
steps.hint: The template should be returned from the setup function. Start with a <div> element that will wrap all your UI elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a template with a container div, ready to hold the search UI elements.
successCriteria: The setup function returns an object with a template property containing a <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the main template structure. The container div will hold all your search UI elements.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a template property from the setup function with a <div> element inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember to add a template section in the return statement. It should contain a <div> element as the main container.

steps.title: Add search input field
steps.instruction: Add an input element inside the template with v-model binding to searchQuery and an @input event wired to the debounced search handler.
steps.hint: Use <input> with v-model and @input attributes. The debounced handler should be called on input events.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: input with v-model and event handler
<input v-model="textValue" @input="handleInput" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an input field that updates searchQuery reactively and triggers the debounced search handler on input.
successCriteria: An input element is added with v-model bound to searchQuery and @input wired to the debounced handler.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the search input field with proper v-model binding and event handling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an input, but check if v-model and @input are correctly set up.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input field is missing or not properly configured. Ensure it has v-model and @input attributes.

steps.title: Display search results count
steps.instruction: In the template, add a paragraph that displays the number of search results using the searchResults ref.
steps.hint: You can access the length of searchResults.value to get the count. Use Vue's template syntax to display it.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: displaying array length in a paragraph

Number of items: {{ items.length }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a paragraph displaying the current number of search results, which updates as the search results change.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added to the template that displays the length of searchResults using Vue's template syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a paragraph that displays the search results count. This gives users immediate feedback about how many results their search returned.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're displaying the actual count of searchResults using Vue's template syntax. Check that you're accessing the length property correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph displaying the search results count is missing or incorrect. Remember to use {{ searchResults.length }} in the template to show the current number of results.

steps.title: Display search results list
steps.instruction: Add an unordered list (<ul>) inside your template that iterates through searchResults using v-for and displays each item in a list element (<li>).
steps.hint: Use v-for to loop through searchResults.value and display each result. Remember to add a key attribute.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: rendering a list in Vue
  • {{ item.name }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display a bulleted list of search results below the input field when results are available.
successCriteria: An unordered list (<ul>) is added to the template that uses v-for to iterate through searchResults and displays each item in a <li> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a list to display the search results. The v-for directive correctly iterates through the results array.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added list markup, but check that you're using v-for correctly on searchResults and displaying each item with {{ }} interpolation.

    with v-for="result in searchResults" and each result inside
